## Summary

In 2021, [Lars Doucet](/wiki/lars-doucet/) — a Norwegian-Texan game designer and self-described "pretty serious Georgist" — won **first place** in Scott Alexander's *Astral Codex Ten* Book Review Contest with a review of Henry George's *[Progress and Poverty](/wiki/progress-and-poverty/)*.

research/doucet-acx-book-review.md.name: Lars Doucet
research/doucet-acx-book-review.md.sentence: The review was published on ACX (anonymously, as a contest finalist) on **16 April 2021**; Alexander announced the results, with Doucet's entry taking **first place**, on **10 July 2021**.

research/doucet-acx-book-review.md.name: Lars Doucet
research/doucet-acx-book-review.md.sentence:
It is widely credited as the spark of the **modern Georgism revival** online.

## Why It Matters

Doucet's review reintroduced George's 142-year-old argument to a large, analytically demanding audience — rationalists, effective altruists, and tech readers — who had never taken land seriously as an economic factor.

research/doucet-acx-book-review.md.name: Lars Doucet

Lars Doucet's *"Does Georgism Work?"* series, published on Astral Codex Ten in 2021–22, is the most widely read modern empirical examination of land value taxation.

## Summary

Released **9 January 2023** — "**Lars Doucet — Progress, poverty, Georgism, & why rent is too damn high**" (the show was then still called *The Lunar Society*) — this roughly **1h40m** episode has host Dwarkesh Patel interview [Lars Doucet](/wiki/lars-doucet/), author of *[Land Is a Big Deal](/wiki/land-is-a-big-deal/)*, about Georgism, land value taxation, and assessment.

## Summary

The **Georgist Podcourse** is a structured, 12-part audio course introducing the principles of Georgist economics, produced by [Earthsharing Australia](/wiki/earthsharing-australia/) (with [Karl Fitzgerald](/wiki/karl-fitzgerald/)) and broadcast on community radio.

## Origin and Format

The Podcourse was announced by Karl Fitzgerald on the Earthsharing Australia blog on **3 May 2019**
